questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The education of girls / is a primary concern for the country, / so it should be started early, / isn’t it?

options.text: so it should be started early
is a primary concern for the country

questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is 'isn't it'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• We often use **question tags** when we expect the listener to agree with our statement. In this case, when the statement is **positive**, we use a **negative question tag**.

 
 
• For example: She **is** a doctor, **isn't** she?
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this context, the **modal** that is used is 'should' (positive).
 
• So, we must use a negative question tag (modal). Hence, 'shouldn't it' must be the appropriate question tag used here.
 
• Thus, 'isn't it' must be replaced by 'shouldn't it'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The education of girls is a primary concern for the country, so it should be started early, ***shouldn't it***?

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The lady was furious / to see that no one / were wearing masks / on the road near the shop.

options.text: on the road near the shop

questions.solution:
The erroneous segment is** "were wearing masks"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the usage of "were wearing masks" is incorrect instead of this we need to use "was wearing masks"
 
• In the given sentence, the subject for the verb "was" is "no one" which is singular in nature hence, we need to use a singular verb. So the correct verb is "was"
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• **The author provides** no documentary references to support her assertions. (The subject is "the author" hence, the verb should be singular i.e. "provides")
 
 

**So the correct sentence is-** *The lady was furious to see that no one **was wearing** masks on the road near the shop.*

questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

__Unless we sat__ in an incorrect posture, we may strain our back.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: If we sit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 'If' is used in sentences in which one thing only happens or is true when another thing happens or is true.
 
• In this context, it is said that if someone sits in an incorrect posture (one thing happens), he/she may strain his/her back (another thing happens).
 
• Also, the sentence is a **conditional sentence. **A conditional sentence begins with 'If'.
 
• If the condition is in the **present tense **(sit), then its result should be in the **future** (denoted by 'may').
 
• The incident that happens first or was supposed to happen first takes a **present tense** (sit) when ‘will/shall/can/may’ is present in the main clause (strain).

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***If we sit***__ in an incorrect posture, we may strain our back.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The three types of conditional sentences (with examples) are given in the table.

 
 

 I
 If I study
 I may pass the exam
 
 

 II
 If I studied
 I might pass the exam
 
 

 III
 If I had studied
 I might have passed the exam

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The president forced / to leave the country / when the people rose up against / the government.

options.text: when the people rose up against

questions.solution:
The erroneous segment is **"The president forced"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the usage of** "forced" is incorrect instead of this we need to use "was forced"**
 
• In the given sentence, the doer for the verb "forced" is somebody else hence, we need to use a passive voice sentence. The president hasn't left the country he was forced to do it. Hence, the doer is somebody else.
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• Amazed Spiderman. (Here, the Amazed is a past participle and the doer for this is somebody else hence, we have used the past participle form)
 
 

**So the correct sentence is-** *The president **was forced **to leave the country when the people rose up against the government.*
